title: Fuel Pressure Regulator Control Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: Fuel pressure regulator reports a control circuit fault.
fullDescription:
The fuel pressure regulator maintains rail pressure within calibrated limits. The PCM has detected a control circuit condition - rail pressure deviates from target outside acceptance.

Driving with abnormal rail pressure stresses injectors and can wash cylinder walls.
safetyImpact: Hard start and possible no-start; safe to coast off the road.

fixSteps.title: Pressure test
fixSteps.instruction: Compare scan-tool fuel pressure to gauge.

fixSteps.title: Inspect regulator return
fixSteps.instruction: Check for fuel in the vacuum line if applicable.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Probe at the connector for 5 V reference.

faq.a: Short distances if it starts.
Possible on returnless rails - search for your engine.

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor B Range/Performance
shortDescription: Intake-air temperature sensor B signal out of range.
fullDescription:
The PCM uses IAT sensor B to calculate air density. A out of range reading distorts fueling and ignition timing.

A shorted or open sensor falls back to a default value with reduced fuel economy.
safetyImpact: Increased emissions and slight drivability impact.

faq.a: Yes - sensors are inexpensive.
Rarely.

title: Mass Air Flow Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: Mass Air Flow sensor signal circuit malfunction.
fullDescription:
MAF sensor measures intake air mass for fueling calculations. The PCM detects a circuit malfunction condition that breaks the speed-density backup model.

Dirty MAF wires are the leading cause - cleaning often resolves the fault.
safetyImpact: Reduced power and high fuel use; no immediate safety risk.

fixSteps.title: Inspect ducting
fixSteps.instruction: Check for leaks between MAF and throttle body.

faq.a: Yes - clean MAF before replacing.
Aftermarket ones often misread - prefer OEM.

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Malfunction
shortDescription: Vehicle speed sensor signal missing.
fullDescription:
The VSS provides vehicle speed for cruise control, ABS, and transmission shift logic. A missing signal can disable cruise and cause harsh shifts.

Often the cluster, ABS module, or transmission output sensor is the culprit.
safetyImpact: Cruise control disabled; transmission may shift harshly.

fixSteps.title: Inspect tone ring
fixSteps.instruction: Look for missing teeth or debris.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: AC voltage at sensor with wheels turning.

faq.a: Often yes - ABS uses its own wheel sensors.
Drive with care - shift quality may suffer.

title: OBD-II Monitor Testing Not Complete
shortDescription: OBD-II readiness monitor: monitors have not run.
fullDescription:
The PCM uses readiness flags to indicate that all emissions monitors have completed at least one full cycle. This code states monitors have not run.

Usually clears after a full drive cycle - it is not a hardware fault.
safetyImpact: Vehicle may not pass smog until monitors complete - no immediate driving risk.

fixSteps.title: Investigate any monitor that will not run

faq.a: Battery was disconnected or codes were cleared recently.
Drive a complete OEM cycle - usually 50-100 miles of mixed driving.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B Malfunction
shortDescription: Throttle/pedal position sensor B malfunction.
fullDescription:
Modern drive-by-wire systems use redundant TPS/APP sensors. The B-channel sensor reports malfunction, so the PCM derates throttle response.

Limp-home is normal until the sensor pair agrees again.
safetyImpact: Reduced power and possible limp mode - safe but slow.

fixSteps.title: Read both TPS channels
fixSteps.instruction: They should track inversely or together per spec.

faq.a: Yes in limp - keep RPM low.
TB cleaning sometimes helps; sensor-side faults need replacement.

title: EVAP Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
shortDescription: EVAP system pressure sensor out of range.
fullDescription:
The EVAP pressure/vacuum sensor monitors fuel-tank pressure for leak detection. A out of range reading prevents the EVAP monitor from completing.

Rule out a loose fuel cap before tearing the system apart.
safetyImpact: Will fail emissions tests; no safety impact.

fixSteps.title: Tighten gas cap
fixSteps.instruction: Drive 1-2 cycles to see if it clears.

fixSteps.title: Smoke-test EVAP
fixSteps.instruction: Identify leaks at hoses and joints.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed component
fixSteps.instruction: Cap, hose, or sensor as found.

faq.a: Often yes - try that first.
Yes - no driveability impact.
